name: Gendle & McGrath 2012 replication: 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal, both temporal lobes
origin: Mathew H. Gendle & Megan G. McGrath, Elon University (independent test); device, amygdala signal and coil set-up by Todd Murphy (8 Coil Shakti)
summary: A copy, for blinded self-tests, of the randomized, placebo-controlled test of a commercial God-Helmet-type device: one 30-min session of the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal over both temporal lobes, followed by emotional ratings of 54 colour photographs. In 37 people (20 field, 17 sham) the paper reports that the field changed neither the ratings nor how they depended on the pictures' valence.
notes: Gendle & McGrath 2012: 20 people got 'the hemispherically symmetrical, fast alternating amygdala signal' of the 8 Coil Shakti for 30 min, at volume 50 for men and 36 for women; 17 got sham (Gendle 2012 p.4 [220], p.7 [223]). All sat blindfolded with ear plugs in a dark, silent, windowless room (p.6 [222]). For sham the device was unplugged: with the program off its solenoids still gave 0.1-0.2 uT of hum (p.5 [221]). Afterwards each rated 54 images alone, 27 s per image, on six 10-cm visual analogue scales (p.5 [221], p.7 [223]). The vendor's file is not published, so the signal is rebuilt: the project's rising sweep, 230 points of 3 ms, one every 4.5 s (this project's choice). Its point values were never published as numbers, and the paper does not state the signal speed. The coils form a cross of four per side (FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and mirrors, this project's reading); the signal switches between the top-bottom and the front-back pairs every 0.5 s, with one coil of each pair reversed. One intensity serves everyone; the paper used two volumes. The paper measured 0.1-1.0 uT RMS with a handheld Gaussmeter in the centre of the headpiece, about 9 cm from the solenoids (p.11 [227]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. 1 uT there is about 0.02 uT at 9 cm from one coil (extrapolated), 5 to 50 times below the measured range. Support: one study, 37 people. Participants were blind; the experimenter was not (p.6-7 [222-223]). No participant reported unusual perceptual experiences (p.9 [225]). The study measured reactions to pictures, not mood. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, a psychiatric condition or medication, or migraine; stop on fear or distress.
setting: In the paper: a padded sleeping blindfold and foam ear plugs in a dark, silent, windowless room for 30 min, in sessions between 12 and 7 pm; the pictures were rated afterwards. A helper who is blind to the condition can start the Blind session and present the photographs.
schedule: One 30-min session per person in the original. Self-test: a fixed number of Blind sessions decided in advance, at least 72 h apart (the vendor's spacing rule), each with the same picture procedure.
source: Gendle & McGrath 2012, Can the 8-coil Shakti alter subjective emotional experience?
